A read of 11 bytes moves the search on 1 byte and repeats 10, so a run of 11-byte reads counts 11 times what whole reads count. Reads of 12 count 6 times, and reads of 13 count 4.3 times. That spends the document's EndStreamSearchPasses budget (4 x file length). Once it is spent, NextSignificant (PdfFileReader.cs:2048) returns -1. The threat model says 'an endstream in a comment that waits is decided as whole reads decide it'. The exception holds only once some window holds the keyword whole, which needs reads of 9 bytes or more across it. Reads of 8 bytes or fewer, or a source whose reads stop at an offset inside the keyword, miss a keyword in a comment like any other. The search then ends elsewhere, such as at the next header. The 'but for' reads as if such a keyword cannot be missed. What is exact is that once a keyword waits, its decision does not depend on the reads: every cut outside the keyword gives the whole-read result.

findings.claim: When an offset falls short of its section, the search near that offset (TryRelocateXRefSection) can find the word xref, or the header of an object giving /Type /XRef, at the start of a line inside an object's stream data, such as an uncompressed embedded file. It takes that place for the section found moved, though no load ever lexes stream data. The same happens on a line inside an object's dictionary or array. Because the nearest such place ends the search (R1-Q1), the reader reports a section that cannot be read: Warning xref.section-unreadable and Error xref.section-malformed, both blamed on the file. The real section, a little farther on, is never read. The index is then rebuilt at opening, which brings back an object the update freed; for an /XRefStm, the older table's row stands and an older revision is served. Main dropped such places, since they are Malformed and not cut by a guard, and read the real section. R2 [2]'s line test excludes only comments and strings, while the principle it settled is that a word no load reads as a token declares no section. Stream data is never lexed. The threat model's #171 Known-gaps entry names, for this search, only strings an earlier line opened, so this case is neither tracked nor documented. Present at 8ba4589 as well: not a round 5 regression. It entered with 0353e24 (R1-Q1).
